slot.brief: Source moving toward then away from a stationary observer at the same speed; ask the ratio of the two observed frequencies.

stem: A source emits sound of frequency $f$ and moves at $30$ m s$^{-1}$ toward and then away from a stationary observer. If the speed of sound is $330$ m s$^{-1}$, what is the ratio of the observed frequencies during approach and recession?

verdicts.working: For a moving source, the ratio is \(f_{\text{approach}}/f_{\text{recession}}=(330+30)/(330-30)=6/5\).

working:
$f_{\text{app}}=f\dfrac{330}{330-30}=\dfrac{11f}{10}$
$f_{\text{rec}}=f\dfrac{330}{330+30}=\dfrac{11f}{12}$
$\dfrac{f_{\text{app}}}{f_{\text{rec}}}=\dfrac{6}{5}$

Independent check: For a moving source, the ratio is \(f_{\text{approach}}/f_{\text{recession}}=(330+30)/(330-30)=6/5\).
